metadata.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes (Kingma & Welling, 2013)
metadata.framework: variational inference for deep latent-variable models via the reparameterization trick
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1312.6114.

nodes.name: Latent variable model
nodes.statement: A directed graphical model with observed variable $\mathbf{x}$ and continuous latent variable $\mathbf{z}$. The generative process: $\mathbf{z} \sim p_\theta(\mathbf{z})$ (prior, e.g., $\mathcal{N}(0,I)$), $\mathbf{x} \sim p_\theta(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{z})$ (likelihood parameterized by a neural network). The marginal likelihood $p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) = \int p_\theta(\mathbf{z}) p_\theta(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{z}) d\mathbf{z}$ is intractable.

nodes.name: Intractable posterior and recognition model
nodes.statement: The true posterior $p_\theta(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x})$ is intractable. Introduce an approximate posterior (recognition/inference model) $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x})$, parameterized by $\phi$ (e.g., a neural network encoder mapping $\mathbf{x}$ to parameters of a Gaussian over $\mathbf{z}$).

nodes.name: Evidence lower bound (ELBO)
nodes.statement: The ELBO (variational lower bound on the log-marginal-likelihood): $\mathcal{L}(\theta, \phi; \mathbf{x}) = \mathbb{E}_{q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x})}[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{z})] - D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x}) \| p_\theta(\mathbf{z})) \le \log p_\theta(\mathbf{x})$. The gap is $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x}) \| p_\theta(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x})) \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Reparameterization trick
nodes.statement: To obtain low-variance gradients of $\mathcal{L}$ w.r.t. $\phi$, reparameterize $\mathbf{z} = g_\phi(\boldsymbol{\epsilon}, \mathbf{x})$ where $\boldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim p(\boldsymbol{\epsilon})$ is a noise source independent of $\phi$. For Gaussian $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x}) = \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\sigma}^2 I)$: $\mathbf{z} = \boldsymbol{\mu} + \boldsymbol{\sigma} \odot \boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ with $\boldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,I)$. Gradients $\nabla_\phi \mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}[f(\mathbf{z})] = \mathbb{E}_{p(\boldsymbol{\epsilon})}[\nabla_\phi f(g_\phi(\boldsymbol{\epsilon}, \mathbf{x}))]$ can now be estimated by Monte Carlo.

nodes.name: Stochastic Gradient Variational Bayes (SGVB) estimator
nodes.statement: The SGVB estimator of the ELBO: $\tilde{\mathcal{L}}(\theta, \phi; \mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{L} \sum_{l=1}^{L} \log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{z}^{(l)}) - D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x}) \| p_\theta(\mathbf{z}))$ where $\mathbf{z}^{(l)} = g_\phi(\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{(l)}, \mathbf{x})$ and $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{(l)} \sim p(\boldsymbol{\epsilon})$. In practice $L=1$ suffices with large enough mini-batches.

nodes.name: Auto-encoding variational Bayes (AEVB) algorithm
nodes.statement: The AEVB algorithm: (1) Sample a mini-batch $\mathbf{x}^{(i)}$ from the dataset. (2) Sample $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ from $p(\boldsymbol{\epsilon})$. (3) Compute the SGVB estimator $\tilde{\mathcal{L}}$. (4) Compute gradients $\nabla_{\theta,\phi} \tilde{\mathcal{L}}$ via backpropagation through the reparameterized $\mathbf{z}$. (5) Update $\theta, \phi$ with SGD/Adam. Repeat until convergence.

nodes.name: Gaussian encoder and decoder (VAE architecture)
nodes.statement: In the specific VAE architecture: the encoder outputs $\boldsymbol{\mu}_\phi(\mathbf{x}), \log \boldsymbol{\sigma}^2_\phi(\mathbf{x})$ parameterizing $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x}) = \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_\phi, \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2_\phi))$. The decoder outputs parameters of $p_\theta(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{z})$ (Bernoulli for binary data or Gaussian for continuous data). The KL term $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_\phi \| p_\theta(\mathbf{z}))$ has a closed-form expression when both are Gaussian.

nodes.name: ELBO decomposition
nodes.statement: For any $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x})$: $\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) = D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x}) \| p_\theta(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x})) + \mathcal{L}(\theta, \phi; \mathbf{x})$. Since $D_{\mathrm{KL}} \ge 0$, the ELBO is a lower bound. Maximizing the ELBO jointly in $\theta$ and $\phi$ simultaneously maximizes the marginal likelihood and minimizes the posterior approximation gap.

nodes.name: Unbiased low-variance gradient estimator via reparameterization
nodes.statement:
The SGVB estimator $	ilde{\mathcal{L}}$ provides unbiased gradients of $\mathcal{L}$ with respect to both $	heta$ and $\phi$: $
abla_{	heta,\phi} 	ilde{\mathcal{L}} = 
abla_{	heta,\phi} \mathcal{L} + O(1/\sqrt{L})$ in the Monte Carlo sense. Unlike the score-function (REINFORCE) estimator $
abla_\phi \mathbb{E}_q[f] = \mathbb{E}_q[f 
abla_\phi \log q]$, the reparameterized estimator has substantially lower variance, enabling practical training.
conclusions: Unbiased gradient estimator for both encoder and decoder parameters
Low variance compared to REINFORCE-style estimators
Practical SGD training of deep generative models

nodes.name: MNIST and Frey Face generation
nodes.statement: VAE trained on MNIST and Frey Face datasets. Demonstrates ability to generate realistic samples, learn meaningful latent representations, and achieve competitive marginal likelihood bounds ($\le -86.76$ nats on MNIST test set).
